channel.title: Jasper's Agent Watch
channel.description: Daily notes on AI agents and agent context: fast-growing GitHub projects, papers, and why they spread.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Weekly · 2026-W43 (2026-10-17 ~ 2026-10-23)
item.description:
• The reverse-engineering Agent morluto/rea gained +106,341 this week, with 368,637 stars, making it the fastest-growing project of the week. The REA post on HN has 814 points, but it was posted on 10-10.
  • Skills remain the biggest source of traffic: cloudflare/security-audit-skill gained ≈+4,040 this week, and a single recommendation tweet got 7,010 likes. anthropics/claude-plugins-official gained +5,649 this week, and Epic's Unreal plugin tweet got 5,186 likes.
  • Context infrastructure keeps heating up: code knowledge graphs (graphify), tool output compression (context-mode, headroom), cross-Agent memory (ai-memory, agent-beacon), and local retrieval (xerj) are all on the charts.
  • On the paper side, the KV cache is becoming a controllable resource for Agents (Cache Engineering for Agents), and memory is becoming "native" (MemT-1.0). Harness self-evolution is the hottest term.
  • The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin ecosystem is taking shape, with free models and context visualization plugins on the charts. Multi-Agent parallel management (Orca, +9,401 this week) and Agent security runtimes (NVIDIA OpenShell, 377 points on HN) are also drawing attention.

item.title: Agent Community Buzz & Growth Attribution · 2026-10-25
item.description:
• morluto/rea +5,896/day, #1 for the second day in a row (see 10-24 report, when it was +5,465). Today's organic discussion shifted to "Did Anthropic add reverse-engineering restrictions to Claude?": one post from @0x0SojalSec got ❤11,831 👁799,288, and one from @Pirat_Nation got ❤4,934 👁267,842. The "restriction" claim comes from users relaying it second-hand. The data contains no official confirmation from Anthropic.
  • cloudflare/security-audit-skill +2,744/day, up from yesterday's +2,177. Organic discussion 👁1,027,652 against only 👁35 from influencer listicles, still the cleanest case of organic spread.
  • The "free model" chain is showing legal and compliance risk. dsh-our-free-model is at +1,767/day, and it was also reported to have received a suspected forged "lawyer's letter" (accusing it of reverse-engineering Tencent's WorkBuddy). yetone/magpie (+670/day) also uses WorkBuddy's free DeepSeek.
  • Multi-harness orchestration is the new hot topic. HarnessRouter lets Grok Bot dispatch Codex, Hermes, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness and others (@_avichawla ❤1,105 👁105,097, with hype copy). Orca and Google Harness² are moving in the same direction.
  • Two projects on the chart have almost no visible X discussion: Nutlope/hallmark (+1,477/day) and makecindy/cindy (+719/day). The source of their growth can't be determined from the data.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-10-25
item.description:
• Harness becomes a hot topic: "Self-Evolving Agent Harness" (👍99, GitHub 387★) and Self-HPO both discuss letting scaffolding such as prompts, memory, and workflows evolve on its own with weights fixed, or optimizing it alternately with the policy.
  • Multi-session context enters RL training: Mosaic treats multi-session trajectories produced by context compaction and sub-agent forking as the training target, closing the mismatch between training and inference.
  • Memory research shifts to "can it improve future actions": MCCL and MemPilot both stop treating memory as a passive retrieval cache. The former stresses evaluating behavioral gains, and the latter curates memory on demand.
  • Environment synthesis and GUI/computer-use agents are another main thread: MAI-Gym, OpenGCUA, WildAWM, and OpenMobile-2 all work on scalable training environments, evaluation, and open full stacks.
  • A RAG compositionality evaluation gives a counterintuitive result: Techniques that work individually see their gains shrink sharply when stacked (predicted +47%, measured +17%).

item.title: Agent Community Buzz & Growth Attribution · 2026-10-24
item.description:
• cloudflare/security-audit-skill is at +2,177/day. It's driven almost entirely by organic discussion. A single recommendation from @jurbed (14,574) got ❤7,958 👁530,393, making it the strongest organic spread today.
  • Security and offense/defense is the most concentrated theme today: Cloudflare's audit skill, NVIDIA SkillSpector, Google mantis, OpenAI's Codex check skill, and morluto/rea for reverse engineering. rea is at +5,465/day, the top of the chart, but all of its exposure comes from listicles.
  • Context and token cost remain a headline selling point: xerj (its official benchmark claims 2.7× fewer output tokens), graphify (knowledge graph), ponytail (less code written). One item in xerj's own case study actually cost more.
  • DeepSeek Harness is at +1,019/day, with a dsh plugin ecosystem around it and a third-party "free models" plugin (+2,120/day). That plugin's author warns "don't share private content," which is a privacy risk.
  • Influencer listicles are still a star amplifier: the graphify listicle/hype posts reached 👁302,150, and Opus 5.5 video projects such as lemo-opuscar reached 👁641,074, but real usage feedback is far smaller than the exposure.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-10-24
item.description:
• Context management for long-horizon agents is shifting from "compressing history" to "organizing context around reusable progress". CarryOn improves results on OSWorld 2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus by 5.8% and 7.0%, while using 51.9% and 22.9% fewer tokens.
  • Context compression and subagent forking are starting to enter RL training. Mosaic takes "multi-session trajectories" as its training setting, which maps directly to compaction and subagent forking at inference time.
  • Harness is a hot topic: a theoretical framework for self-evolving harnesses, Self-HPO, which alternately optimizes harness and policy, HexaShell, a "thin harness", and OpenGCUA, which shifts decisions from harness rules to the model.
  • The way skills are learned has been redesigned: Socratic Skill Learning lets a Student write skills while practicing under expert guidance.
  • Evaluation is moving from "final success" to "process validity": BizBench shows that looking only at outcomes hides rule-violating execution.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context on GitHub · 2026-10-23
item.description:
• morluto/rea leads by a wide margin at +5853/day, with stars now at 371,232. "Using agents for reverse engineering" is today's strongest vertical, and similar projects Zfinix/eleven and awesome-reverse-engineering are also on the new-repo list.
  • The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin ecosystem is taking shape quickly: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness has 259,225 stars, and popular projects such as rea, archify and ruflo all carry the dsh-plugin tag.
  • Codebase indexing / local retrieval is heating up: xerj is at +938/day and graphify at +858/day. Both emphasize local-first, no vector DB or a single binary, and plug into many agents via MCP/Skill.
  • Skills remain the main distribution format: cloudflare/security-audit-skill is at +2038/day and ponytail at +1292/day, while established projects like ECC and superpowers keep growing.
  • Agent runtimes and multi-agent management are drawing attention: NVIDIA/OpenShell is at +978/day and stablyai/orca at +848/day.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-10-23
item.description:
• Cache and context are starting to be designed together: Cache Engineering for Agents lets the agent control the KV cache directly (drop / repos) instead of rewriting the trajectory prefix, cutting average cost by 27.7% versus threshold-triggered summarization.
  • Memory moves inside the model: MemT-1.0 makes memory part of the model's computation, with 66× less persistent storage than a full-context KV cache at 128K history.
  • Rethinking "complex memory": Raw-RAG ranks first on several long-term memory benchmarks, questioning whether structured agent memory is necessary; meanwhile a survey-style work, MCCL, argues memory should be judged by "whether it improves future actions."
  • The harness becomes a training target: CoEvo-RSI, Self-HPO, Harness Scaling, Self-Evolving Agent Harness and others work on co-evolving or diversifying the harness and the model during training.
  • Long-horizon context folding meets training: CarryOn (object-oriented context) and Mosaic (multi-session RL) address the multi-session trajectories produced by compression / sub-agents from the runtime side and the training side, respectively.

item.title: Agent Community Buzz & Growth Attribution · 2026-10-23
item.description:
• Top daily gainer is morluto/rea (+5,853), but on X it has only 2 listicle posts (combined 👁32,359) and zero organic discussion. The only visible organic buzz is a 10-10 HN post (814 points / 340 comments); the data doesn't show where today's gain came from.
  • Security auditing is today's strongest organic discussion topic: cloudflare/security-audit-skill has 19 organic discussion posts in the past 7 days, combined 👁963,679, including a single recommendation from @jurbed with 👁530,393. Similar topics at the same time include OpenAI's Codex check skill, NVIDIA SkillSpector, and google/mantis.
  • Graphify's exposure comes mainly from influencers: listicle and hype-copy tweets total 👁515,964, while organic discussion is only 👁82,176; two of the large-account tweets share the same opening copy ("It is becoming f*cking dangerous"). Organic discussion centers on how to use the PreToolUse hook and on "inferred edges must be correctable".
  • The DeepSeek Harness ecosystem is heating up: deepseek-harness (+1,127) and the third-party free-model plugin dsh-our-free-model (+2,089) are both on the chart. The latter has only 1 post on X (👁4,678), and its author warns "don't share anything private with it".
  • NVIDIA/OpenShell (+978) is driven by HN: the 10-22 HN post has 458 points / 205 comments, and only one Spanish-language listicle on X mentions it.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context on GitHub · 2026-10-22
item.description:
• Context tools lead Trending: Graphify (codebase knowledge graph) is +1,407 today, Headroom (tool output compression) +552, and Agent Beacon (cross-harness memory layer) +226.
  • Agents are becoming skills: cloudflare/security-audit-skill leads at +2,979 today, and plugin / skill repos from Anthropic, Cursor, and Vercel are also on the weekly list.
  • Managing multiple parallel agents is becoming a tooling category: Orca is +1,694 today and +8,705 this week; new repos harp, coucou, and PandaCode all build a unified panel for several coding agents.
  • Memory and retrieval layers are emerging in force: xerj (local search + MCP) is +8,731 this week, ai-memory +2,833 this week, plus engram, agentmemoryrepo, and others.
  • Many rising stars use agent skills for video, animation, and CAD: huashu-motion, onetake, openfilm, solidcraft, and more.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-10-22
item.description:
• KV cache becomes a controllable resource for agents: Cache Engineering (AKV) lets agents drop/repos active KV directly, without changing the prefix or re-prefilling; MemT-1.0 builds memory into the model itself, cutting storage 66x at 128K history.
  • Harness is the hottest word today: OpenVLHarness, CoEvo-RSI, Self-HPO, HarnessPro, Harness Scaling and others center on "harness self-evolution / co-evolution with the model", but Harness-Delta Attribution points out that a considerable share of the gains comes from overfitting.
  • Memory research shifts to "what to store, what to forget": REM, TokenWorth, Anti-Persistence and MemoryTax all question whether "remembering more is better", stressing selective storage and on-demand reconstruction.
  • Security and failure surfaces of context management are exposed: Compaction Laundering shows that flattening role labels during compaction lets forged user instructions get "laundered" into memory; other work shows that harness truncation and retrieval choices directly determine success or failure.
  • Environment synthesis and evaluation keep expanding: WildAWM, CoworkEnv and Interlock synthesize training environments, while AdaExploreBench, MMEnterprise-Bench and others add evaluation benchmarks.
